reviews.comment: Took days to respond to a help request over a bug, he responded the day before due and told me he couldn't figure out how to help or fix it, but still told me he'd grade me badly if I don't. Routes for you fail.

Disorganized in everything he does and just a bad teacher overall. Exams are unfair and unclear. The group project is paramount to passing, but for teaching a "Software Development" class it's clear he knows nothing about the languages he teaches and WILL NOT help you with even basic issues. AWFUL professor, AWFUL class, AWFUL experience.

I'm in my third year at RIT, and I've never had a professor so bad that I had to write a review Martinez is condescending, threatening, and rude. Description of assignments is vague, points are taken off for not doing arbitrary tasks decided after submission. Quizzes and tests have low average, he made everyone make a rap video to get extra credit

This is just not a fun class to be in (which contradicts his mantra). Not too hard at first but ramps up considerably during the project assignment. Martinez himself is fine, but I would avoid this class if you already have a heavy workload.
Talks way too much and doesn't have good lectures

One of my favorite professors of all time honestly. He was a very enthusiastic and engaging professor and was very connected with the students in the class. Definitely made me feel heard and was very understanding. The course itself was difficult but its not Martinez's fault. He made a hard course more fun and easy to manage especially for 8am.

Can be tough, but he's very good at teaching the material. He knows what he is talking about very well and is always willing to help. He makes you participate but you will learn better that way. Worth it if you want to do well in software engineering.

I would warn that many of the reviews I have seen for Martinez are clearly having a difficult time separating the class from the professor. Martinez is caring and excited to teach this course. I've gained more applicable professional knowledge in this class than any other. He doesn't get to choose the course material, but he does make it more fun.

Professor Martinez is incredibly compassionate; if he notices that a student or group is heading down the wrong path, he will take the time to talk with them. Although it appears that he is strict about the course, the students really benefit from it. Classes are really engaging because of the manner he presents with candies and dresses stakeholder

The course itself was not organized but I found that the professor didn't help with making the course any better. The midterm requires knowing specific information across all of the slides which makes it harder than it needs to be. Also the teacher will not be able to help much if you have an actual coding problem.

He really cares about his students and their success, and it really shows. Lectures may be a little long sometime, but that's from the structure of the course and not Martinez who tries to make them as enjoyable as possible. Definitely participate and you'll be good for the rest of the class. He's tough but good. 10/10 recommend

Wow, bottom-tier professor. I learned literally nothing in his lectures. You can never really tell what is due when because he will change deadlines in class and then not reflect them in myCourses. I hear not all SE professors are like him, but I am happy this is the only SE class CS majors have to take. Avoid him if you can.

This class is as much work as all four other computing classes that I'm taking this semester. It's a lot of assignments, group work, and random project milestones that come way too close together. He's incredibly disorganized, spreading information across an outside website or slack, and constantly runs over time. He's a very harsh grader as welll.

Failed to respond to students in a timely manner & changed exam dates without warning. Even the TA didn't know what was going on. Didn't follow the One Stop Shop & completely changed our final project, not even directly communicating what the new project was to the students. Grades based off other submissions, will require reading ahead.

If I could give this guy a zero, I would. Definitely, one of the worst professors I have ever had. No organization, slow response time, tough grader, etc. He never taught anything in lectures but instead just read off the slides. I I had to teach myself the material as the class progressed. Avoid Martinez at all costs!

In short, this class is not a 3 credit class. You make a full stack web application with frameworks and technologies you have not used before, which is 50% of your grade. The other 50% is made up of tedious random quizzes and exams that you cannot study for as they overlap with the project work that you literally have to self teach yourself.

Whoever gives this professor above a 1 is crazy! If I could give a zero I would. This guy has no organization, responds to messages at a snail's pace, and doesn't teach the material at all. I had to learn the material on my own. This class has a workload that is way more than 3 credits. Strict grader as well. Avoid Martinez at all costs!
Kenn means well and does a good job keeping the class engaged, but If you ask this man a difficult question, he will speak in riddles and try to have you come up with your own answer to it.
Very hard time in this class but it's very hard material. Martinez did his best to keep the class engaged and participating in the lecture. He clearly cares if the students know the material or not.

I had Kenneth Martinez for Sun 101 and it was terribly. The lectures have noting to do with the group work and the homework requirements are not in the same spot as the submission. He also drops things on his students last minute, like "learn html for next weeks project". Overall super unorganized and a terrible lecturer.

I have very mixed feelings about him. I took this class a while back. Pros? He's super accessible and somewhat understanding. My group for the checkers project put in no work, so he bumped my grade up heavily because I did 95% of the work and couldn't get a good score on my own. Cons? Not really a great professor. Makes the class hard for no reason
I would rather drop out of college than take another class with Martinez. ��

Everything bad I have to say is about the material (which is being changed next semester) and NOT Professor Martinez. I started out hating this course but grew to really love it. Martinez tries his best to make the class entertaining and fun. If possible, I would highly recommend taking this course with friends to ensure you are in a good group.

I heard rumors of Martinez being a tough professor, but SWEN256 being not so code oriented probably helped that it wasn't as bad as expected. Mostly just lectures and group work so the class wasn't too bad. Everything was pretty fair game in terms of things that showed up on exams and assignments.

First off, he's probably a nice guy and he really tries to get students engaged. but avoid this class like the plauge. There is an unreasonable amount of work. he rarely goes over things and he assigns quizzes for things he hasn't even gone over yet to "save time". Any question you ask he will deflect by saying "that's just meat and potatoes".
He's just bad

Required more work in one elective than in every other class I had combined. Would regularly have multiple papers due every week in addition to significant amounts of reading he would quiz you on. Intentionally makes vague and changing requirements to "prepare us for the real world". Will also spy on communications and call you out in class.
He makes an intro course 10x more difficult than it should be. Micromanaging students on Zoom is not how you teach a class well.

You won't learn a lot from Prof. Martinez, and what you do learn is probably wrong. In his lectures he would teach blatantly wrong information, and then these incorrect statements were defended as "subjective". Exams are not fair and questions are too open ended. Do not take this professor.

May god bless your soul if you get him for senior project. Easily made me and my three other teammates' last year of college living hell. Constantly lectured us about dumb things all the time to the point where none of us wanted to work on our senior project any longer past the second month or so. Made me leave RIT with a horrible taste in my mouth

Taking a class with Martinez is like taking an online class. Lots of students will fall behind because he doesn't emphasize how much he expects you to read every resource that is provided on the website, or just mentioned in general. He's a very reasonable human and will give extensions. Overall I think he could focus on less outside learning .

Took this class because I had almost no other options for an elective. It's worse than the rumors. You have almost 3/4 things due in a given week on top of the group assignment where some put in 40 hours a week into. Avoid this class if you value mental health. Do not take with more than 12 credits. If you've been on coop, you'll learn nothing
Seems okay for 101. Not always clear when lecturing.

Never finished a test in the allotted time. Cares about your health but not about the clarity of the assignment. Interesting guy. Will hook you up with forms of career opportunity. Throws candy at you. Keep him close for career opportunities but don't purposefully take classes with him unless you like a challenge, and hate your GPA.
I think he should stick to only teaching SWEN101 and should drop the rest of the classes because he cant teach

He's a really nice guy. My group (4 including myself) never finished a test in the alotted time slot. Lectures are extremely boring and will call out your name if you fall asleep Responds to emails in a timely manner Definitely avoid taking his classses

Terrible. When go to Office hours and ask for help says "I don't want to give you any hints." Spends all class trying to draw nice pictures instead of actually teaching the class. Poor time management during class, we never get as far as we are supposed to. Class could be very interesting but I find it difficult to learn with Kenn. AVOID

Martinez Is one of the least helpful professors I've ever had at RIT. He claims to be accessible outside of class but takes forever to answer e-mails and seems to nap during his office hours. In class he rambles and doesn't seem to truly know what he's talking about, often answering questions with questions of his own. Avoid at all costs.

Convoluted, unhelpful, inaccessible, and unrealistic. Honestly one of my top three least favorite professors I have had in college. Stay away if you can! I heard horror stories about the class and didn't have a choice but to take 383 with him. I thought others were exaggerating. They weren't. He seems like a nice guy, just not a good teacher.
The worst professor in the RIT. He is not helpful at all!! Do not take him!!!

Martinez has no idea what he's talking about. When lecturing, he can't answer any of the students questions and just abstracts ideas into buzzwords like "Cloud" and if he doesn't understand the buzzword, he'll just make food analogies, like "meat and potatoes". This professor gets away with incompetence by hiding behind a "customer hat".

The class is 99% online even though it is supposed to be in class only. You get 0 feedback on quizzes which are given before every class on material not covered yet. He will never meet with you even for office hours and takes multiple days to answer any email. Has been my worst experience with any class or teacher at RIT.

Okay, this class is way more difficult than other sections. However, you will learn a lot, and he cares a lot about you as a student. There is a ton work outside of class and not too clear-cut things to do. The effort sometimes does not correlate with the grade. Other teachers make this class far easier. Beware of extra requirements.
He's a great professor for this class, as he is very knowledgeable and passionate about the material. It's a freshman intro course so you shouldn't be really worried about the course material at all.

Martinez is an excellent professor. He is dedicated and does his best to make the class enjoyably, comical and educational. His tests are fairly tough so make sure to study and attend SSE review sessions. For 261, the textbook was VERY expensive and only used 5 times. Important Note: He will give you candy with every test.
Passionate about work. Teaching of said work needs work. Though the course itself is not for everyone and is loaded with content.
Project guidance was mostly clear, but specific assignment instructions were routinely misunderstood by most or all of the class.

He is very funny and an excellent lecture. Lectures are clear and concise. He always adds a little flare to the class and he sometimes gives students with candy if you visit him during office hours. I cannot wait to take a class with him in the future!

Ken was alright. Firstly, it's not his fault he has to teach such a useless class. Speaking on him though, some days he would be fun and engaging and other days he'd be very annoying and slightly rude to us. Not much work though, you basically get a grade for showing up and participating in the easy group activities.

Professor Martinez is excellent. He is capable of motivating his students to do their best. Doesn't look down on his students, simply wants to see them succeed. The class was extremely helpful and I think it is one of the most useful classes I have taken. If you truly want to learn from a class, I recommend Martinez

Tries to come off as a cool and chill guy but in reality he is rude, arrogant and self centered. For someone teaching a class about project management he is amazingly unorganized and displays many of the qualities he tells others to avoid. His mismanagement often resulted in confusion and resulted in class ending with unanswered questions. Avoid!

Pros: You'll learn a lot about software engineering and he'll spend every minute of class trying to engage you. Cons: He can be incredibly rude and arrogant. He thinks he's the smartest guy he's ever met. He can be quite unclear about assignments and is a very tough grader. Overall: Stay away from him unless you're willing to ignore his personality
Fantastic professor. Really cares about both the subject matter and the students.

He has two modes: Software engineering philosophy and programming teacher. He is great at explaining good practices and the software industry, but he gets distracted by this when actually trying to teach programming languages. I found the class easy, but others were confused by his banter. I enjoyed this class.

Professor Martinez is one of the most inspiring teachers I have ever met. He tosses out candy if you are active in class or you're falling asleep in class. He is super helpful when you have questions about the project. He does a very good job acting as a real life customer for the project. Overall, Take SWEN-261 with him and you won't regret it.

Professor Martinez is a great professor. He keeps the class and its content very relatable, easy to understand, and never manages to lose your attention or put you to sleep. He comes off as a professor who genuinely cares about his students and actually wants to see them learn and succeed. He is a good professor I'd recommend to anyone.

If you get a bad group you're screwed. The entire class is mostly one large project. I told to him early on that my group wasn't helping and his response was well talk to them. At the conclusion of the project I used the git logs to prove I wrote just under 90% of the code and he still gave me a D. Only responds to emails if you CC advisor.

Warning if you're taking his class: He'll expect you to meet with your team and begin coding your project long before it says on the schedule. His slideshows are boring if you already know something about software engineering. Expects a lot of busy work done for each step of the project.

Once you understand where he is coming from he is a great professor. His teaching has made my work experience wildly profitable. Although some of the work may be busy work, it's one of those things where you say, "that's what he meant, I get it now."
I've always gotten along with my teachers but this guy not at all I hate him with every fiber of my being
One of the best members of the SE department. He is clear, understandable, and fair in grading. The project could use a little bit of improvement and was overly ambiguous.

Martinez was unusually harsh in providing feedback. Also the problem seemed to that he took a hands off approach this time, but failed to provide any kind of aid when some signs of distress were shown. Even if the sponsor is happy with the project he would only focus on what went wrong than what went right.

Easily one of the worst professors I've had at RIT. He preaches about the 80/20 principle, but doesn't practice it in teaching the course. Exams are unreasonably difficult only because we're not explicitly told what to study. I was very interested in Software Process, but this professor completely destroyed my interest in the subject.

The Buzzword king!! Still takes points off even if you have the right answer. He just reads off of slides and picks on random people for his own pleasure. He is also unhelpful outside of class. Final verdict: avoid like the plague!

Awful professor. In order to even pass the course you have to quote the book, he takes off lots of points even if your answer is completely correct but not word-for-word what the book says. Questions also have a lot of hidden meaning, he doesn't ask the questions for the answers he expects. Avoid at all costs!

Horrible experience, very negative in his feedback. Always focuses on the negative aspect of your work and doesn't understand that you have other responsibilities. Even if the sponsor was happy with our product, He would always find something to bash on us about (in a polite way). I give him that, He is just really disconnected from students

So harsh and unfair! All he cares about is buzzwords and he likes to pick on random people in class. He just gave our team a 70% in a easy project because he didn't like our (perfectly reasonable) variable names, and he finds every little flaw to pick apart. One kid in our group has a stutter and he took off half a letter for that! AVOID HIM!!!!!!!

A good lecturer, he often makes students think a little outside the box. He was engaging and managed to keep me awake during the classes. During team sessions he provided good insight into how to do better on the projects. The only slight hitch would be his grading. It is a little buzzword bingo, but if you know the material its not a problem.

He is good at lecturing. However, he is a harsh grader. Asks a lot. thinks that whole your life is his class. grades slowly and cuts a lot of points for nothing. Definitely, suggest to not take him if you have a chance.

Worst teaching experience at RIT. Overwhelms you with 100+ pages of required readings weekly, and tests are based off of that. Very very inconsistent with grading and incredibly harsh. Will circle buzzwords on an exam and you get points based off of that. I have learned almost nothing in this class.

Martinez is absolutely unreasonable and hypocritical. Expecting all assignments to be turned in by the deadline with absolutely no exceptions, he himself fails to return graded assignments within the time frame that he promises. Additionally, when he fails to clarify an assignment's due date he assumes no responsibility.
Worst experience at RIT. Refuses to give partial credit. Looks for "buzz words" on your answers when grading exams. Got a C in what should have been an easy A class...avoid at all costs!
Terrible teaching style, very unfair grading. Worst experience of my RIT career so far.
No Comments
